Patients in many parts of the country have been left unable to access their GP surgery online after a tech firm went into administration.

Silicon Practice ran digital services, including websites, online booking and consultations, for around 500 practices in England – just under 10% of the total.

Practices across the country, including in London, Gloucestershire and Norfolk , have reported problems. Services in Wales are also affected.

GP leaders said the problem would cause huge disruption, given the scale of online booking that now takes places.

Patients in areas that are affected are being advised they will have to make appointments via the phone. The NHS app is working.

Since last year , all practices in England have had to offer online appointment booking. Currently, more than 40% of appointments are made that way.

An NHS England spokesperson said while "the majority" of GP practice websites were running as normal, some using Silicon Practice will be affected.

"If your GP practice website is unavailable and you need help, you should contact your practice by phone or in person as usual."

Affected practices have been contacted by NHS England with advice on how to maintain business continuity and minimise the impact on patient care.

Silicon Practice ran the digital tool FootFall, which it advertised as reducing patient phone calls to practices by 30%, by working to "free your reception team from routine admin and manage demand more efficiently. Proven in 1,000+ GP practices across the UK".

Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, president of the Royal College of GPs, said: "GP practice websites are an increasingly important way for patients to access care, book appointments and find information about the services available to them.

"When websites are not working, it can be hugely disruptive for patients and place additional pressures on already stretched practice teams.

"It is vital that any disruption to practice websites is addressed promptly to ensure patients are able to access care."

She said affected practices must receive prompt, practical support from NHS England and local NHS organisations to restore their websites, minimise disruption and ensure patients know how to contact their practice and access the care they need in the meantime.

Are you affected by issues covered in this story? Share your experiences.

Just over a week ago, we released Granite Switch 4.1 , showing that our modular Switch architecture lets you configure a language model with specialized, cache-efficient adapters — adding new expertise on a single endpoint.

Granite Switch 4.1.1 is a patch release. The version number means what it means in software: fully backwards compatible with 4.1, no migration, incremental improvements under the hood.

While we are excited about these new features, what is notable is the speed and efficiency with which our teams could release this update. Apart from training the new ASR model and Decision adapter, nothing was recomputed: the base model is untouched. You compose the latest adapters you want and deploy.

This pattern can power far more than patch releases to an IBM-provided model. We're working on tutorials and an Adapter SDK so developers and third-party providers can build their own adapters — iterate on versions, test features, and ship updates the way you ship software. More soon.

Until then, test out our latest models , and try out the new multilingual and punctuation capabilities powering our Speech-to-Decisions demo.

MN202610_4hyj3prfkj.t:
The previous occupant of Ryua's apartment, pictured here, sadly took their own life

From the moment Ryua first walked into her rental apartment in Tokyo she believed it to be haunted.

"When I visited the place for a viewing there was a man standing there, glaring at me," she says.

"Since the estate agent couldn't see him, I realised he must be a ghost."

While someone more squeamish would probably have quickly left the flat never to return, Ryua chose to go ahead and move in.

"I'm a bit of a contrarian, so I decided I wanted to become friends with this glaring male ghost," adds Ryua, who works as an aidoru, a young entertainer, and who doesn't wish to share her surname.

Four years later, and still in the same apartment, she says she continues to experience paranormal activity on a daily basis. She says she hears endless footsteps and the ghost talking.

Ryua says that she shares her Tokyo apartment with a ghost

Although Japan has increasingly marked Halloween , external in recent years, many Japanese people take ghosts seriously all year round. The country has a word, "yuurei", which means a lingering, troubled spirit.

These are the ghosts of people who died in violent or tragic circumstances - those who were murdered, killed themselves, or simply were lonely and died alone. If they died at home, then the belief is that their yuurei won't go away.

For house hunters who are not superstitious or squeamish it means there are big bargains to be found. There is a whole category of dwellings called jiko bukken, which means "stigmatised" or "incident" properties.

Under guidelines issued by the government in 2021, Japanese estate agents must disclose suicide, murder, death by fire, and any death where the body was not discovered for an extended period of time.

For rental properties this information must be disclosed for three years, and it must be revealed indefinitely for any property offered for sale.

By contrast, in the UK there is no legal requirement to reveal that a person died in a property. And in the US, it differs from state to state. , external For example, in California you have to reveal if a person has died in the property in the past three years, while in Arizona and Oregon you do not.

Ryua was told that a man had killed himself in her apartment. It meant that she gets an almost 30% discount on her rent on her tiny, 25 sq m bedsit in the fashionable ward of Setagaya. She says she pays 45,000 yen ($285; £213) a month, instead of what should have been 62,000 yen.

While a house where there had been a murder or suicide would probably be harder to sell or rent out anywhere in the world, Tokyo estate agent Erik Oskamp says that Japanese people are particularly superstitious and averse to stigmatised properties.

"[Even] an apartment next to a cemetery will be difficult to rent out, especially if you can see the tombs from the kitchen," explains Oskamp. "The worst thing is if a suicide has happened in the apartment. Even if somebody has jumped from the roof, many renters will move out. Other issues are a serious crime or a lonely death."

The latter issue, that of a person dying alone, would not generally affect the price of a property in, say, the UK or the US.

But in rural Kagoshima, in Japan's southwest, it enabled Diane Tincher to buy a large three-bedroom house for about half of what would have otherwise been the asking price.

The 69-year-old American has lived in Japan for nearly 40 years, working as a tour guide. She says that the estate agent had been straight with her – there was a heavy discount as an elderly lady had died alone, thereby stigmatising the property.

Tincher paid 20m yen for the house, in a location where similar properties usually sell for up to 45m yen.

"I don't believe in ghosts. But I know that the Japanese are very superstitious," she says. "If there is a ghost I'm thankful to her every day... to live in such a splendid and affordable home."

Diane Tincher says she got a 50% reduction on her home in rural Japan

Researching the house, Tincher had found it on a website called Oshimaland, which lists jiko bukken properties, giving details of the events that occurred. It was launched in 2005 covering Tokyo, before expanding across Japan and then internationally in 2011.

It is crowdsourced, meaning that members of the public add the homes and their details.

Diane Tincher got a huge discount on her home in rural Japan

Teru Oshima, the founder of Oshimaland, says that in the past such properties were "not very attractive options" in Japan.

Yet as house prices have surged in the country in recent years, as well as a big increase in the wider cost of living, one 2025 survey found that more than half of Japanese people would now rent a jiko bukken if it was cheap. , external

Back in Setagaya, Ryua says she is happy living with her ghostly flatmate. "I believe that ghosts were once living human beings, so they deserve our respect," she says.

For support and more information on any of the topics raised in this article, help is available on the BBC Action Line.

Leta zunze ubumwe za Amerika zatangaje ibihano bishya kuri Ministeri y’Ingabo mu Rwanda na Banki yo kubitsa no kwizigama ya Gisirikare izwi nka ZIGAMA CSS, ngo ibihano byafatiwe u Rwanda kubera ko rutubahiriza ibyo rwiyemeje mu gusinya amasezerano y’i Washington.

Itangazo ryo ku itariki 28 Ukwakira, 2026 rivuga ibi bihano riri ku rubuga rwa Deparitoma ishinzwe Umutungo muri America.

Scott Bessent, umunyamabanga w’imari muri America avuga ko biriya bihano bishya ari ‘isezerano rya Perezida Trump ryo kubaza u Rwanda inshingano ku byo rwiyemeje mu masezerano y’i Washington’.

Scott Bessent yagize ati “U Rwanda rugomba guhagarika inkunga yarwo kuri M23, no gukura ingabo zarwo mu burasirazuba bwa Congo.”

Radio RFI ivuga ko ibihano bishya bireba Minisiteri y’Ingabo z’u Rwanda, ndetse n’ikigo cy’imari cya gisirikare Zigama – CSS.

Kubera ibyo bihano, imitungo y’ibibi bigo n’inyungu zabyo muri Leta Zunze Ubumwe za America byafatiriwe.

Scott Bessent avuga ko, ibi bihano bigamije gutuma amasezerano yasinywe i Washington hagati y’u Rwanda na Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo ashyirwa mu bikorwa, dore ko Perezida Donald Trump akunda kuvuga ko ayo masezerano yazanye amahoro.

America ishinja u Rwanda kohereza ingabo muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo na Kivu ya Ruguru, zikaba ziha imyitozo M23, kandi zikanakorana na yo mu kugaba ibitero.

U Rwanda kandi ngo rwohereje intwaro zigezweho zirimo missile, n’ikoranabuhanga rishobora kuyobya indege.

Lucie Mouillaud uhagarariye RFI i Kigali, yasubiyemo amagambo y’Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma y’u Rwanda kuri ibi bihano America yarufatiye.

Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma y’u Rwanda, Yolande Makolo, yagize ati: “Impande zose zigomba kubazwa ibyo ziyemeje. Amasezerano y’i Washington akubiyemo ingingo zisobanutse (…), by’umwihariko kurandura FDLR – umutwe w’abajenosideri ushyigikiwe na leta ya Congo.”

Yolande Makolo akavuga ko kugeza ubu, ibyo biri mu masezerano batarashyirwa mu bikorwa na gato, kandi ko nta kubibaza Congo kwabayeho.

Makolo yakomeje avuga ko U Rwanda rwiteguye gushyira mu bikorwa amasezerano y’i Washington uko yakabaye, ariko bigakorwa na na Congo yemeye gushyira mu bikorwa ibyo yiyemeje kandi n’umuhuza mu kibazo agakora ku buryo buri ruhande rubazwa ibyo rwemeye gukora.

Muri Werurwe, America yari yafatiye ibihano Igisirikare cy’u Rwanda (RDF) na bamwe mu bayobozi bo mu Rwanda barimo General (Rtd) James Kabarebe.

Guverinoma y’u Rwanda na bwo yasohoye itangazo rigenewe abanyamakuru, inenga ko ibihano bifatirwa “uruhande rumwe”, “bikagaragaza ko ukuri kw’ibibera mu ntambara kwirengagijwe.”

America ivuga ko yafatiye ibihano Banki ya Zigama CSS kubera ko yafashije M23 kubona za miliyoni z’amadolari, kandi ikaba yarafashije ko amabuye y’agaciro ya zahabu yo mu bice bigenzurwa n’inyeshyamba agezwa ku isoko.

Ikindi ngo iyi banki yafashije mu kugura intwaro zaba ari iz’ingabo z’u Rwanda cyangwa izijya mu nyeshyamba.

Ibihano bya America uretse gufatira imitungo yose ya Ministeri y’Ingabo mu Rwanda na ZIGAMA CSS yaba iri muri America mu buryo buziguye cyangwa butaziguye, binabuza ibi bigo gukoresha Idolari mu ihererekanya ry’amafaranga mpuzamahanga nk’uko RFI ibivuga.

Urukiko rw’Ibanze rwa Kicukiro rwemeje ko ikirego cya Idrissa Ouedraogo arega umugore we Ishimwe Vestine gifite ishingiro, rutegeka ko umwana babyaranye apimwa ibizamini bya DNA ndetse Idrissa akajya ahabwa amafoto menshi y’umwana.

Uyu mwanzuro watangajwe ku wa Gatatu, tariki ya 28 Ukwakira 2026, ubwo hasomwaga urubanza Idrissa yari yararezemo Vestine, asaba ko hakorwa ibizamini by’uturemangingo ndangasano kugira ngo hamenyekane isano afitanye n’umwana, ndetse agahabwa n’uburenganzira bwo kumubona.

Mu isomwa ry’urubanza, umucamanza yavuze ko Ishimwe Vestine yemeye ibyifuzo bya Idrissa, birimo kumwoherereza amafoto y’umwana no gukorwa kwa DNA, mu rwego rwo kurengera inyungu z’umwana.

Urukiko rwanzuye ko ibizamini bya DNA by’umwana, witwa Ishimwe Nollah, bizafatirwa muri Canada aho ari, bikoherezwa mu Rwanda kugira ngo bihuzwe n’ibya Idrissa.

Byagaragajwe ko ibisubizo bizoherezwa mu Kigo cy’Igihugu gishinzwe ibimenyetso bishingiye ku bumenyi n’ubuhanga bikoreshwa mu butabera (RFI) kugira ngo bisuzumwe.

Urukiko rwashingiye ku ngingo ya 48 y’itegeko rigenga abantu n’umuryango, ndetse n’ubwumvikane bw’impande zombi, rwemeza ko ibyo Idrissa yasabaga bifite ishingiro. Rwanategetse ko ahabwa amafoto menshi y’umwana kurusha ayo yahabwaga mbere.

Uyu mwanzuro uje nyuma y’uko Idrissa yari yitabaje ubutabera asaba ko uburenganzira bwe ku mwana babyaranye bwubahirizwa, hakurikijwe ibyo yari yasabye mu rubanza.

MN202610_gm0i61f02f.t:
An initiative bringing together universities, research organizations, industry, and the open science community to make publicly funded research easier to discover, reuse, and build upon.

Today, we're announcing Project ProtoStar , an initiative to unlock the potential of publicly funded scientific research by making datasets, models, and code more accessible and reusable, particularly for AI-driven research. ProtoStar brings together research institutions, industry, and the open science community to support the release of scientific artifacts in AI-ready, machine-actionable formats, and to demonstrate their value through a series of open challenges. The first challenge, hosted by Carnegie Mellon University , opens on November 2. See How to Participate below.

The initiative's founding partners include Carnegie Mellon University , Purdue University , Georgia Institute of Technology , Arizona State University , and The George Washington University , all working through the Open Forum for AI (OFAI) as the university coalition partner; the Astera Institute ; Hugging Face as the infrastructure partner; and the Open Research Community Accelerator (ORCA) , through its Fostering Innovation Network , as the community partner.

Participating organizations formalize their involvement through a memorandum of understanding supporting the release of suitable scientific datasets, models, and code in AI-ready formats on open infrastructure. Organizations interested in joining Project ProtoStar can reach out to protostar@orcaopen.org .

The U.S. federal government invests approximately $190 billion annually in research and development , and federal policy increasingly expects the results to be shared publicly. Agencies such as the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and National Science Foundation (NSF) have strengthened public-access requirements for funded research publications and require researchers to plan for sharing the underlying data. Hugging Face is among the ten generalist repositories listed by NIH for sharing research data.

But making research publicly available does not automatically make it usable. Scientific datasets, models, and code are often scattered across incompatible systems, stored in static or legacy formats, or released without the documentation, metadata, and provenance needed to understand and reuse them. These limitations make it harder for researchers to build on existing work, and harder still for AI systems to discover, interpret, and combine scientific resources across disciplines.

Project ProtoStar aims to help close this gap by encouraging systematic sharing of publicly funded scientific artifacts in AI-ready formats, supported by open infrastructure and practical publishing guidance. It builds on efforts such as the National Cancer Institute's AI Data-Readiness Challenge and Hugging Face's guide to preparing public-sector data for AI . The goal is to make it easier for research organizations to meet existing public-access expectations while increasing the scientific value of the work they release.

The demand for reusable scientific resources is already evident. Hugging Face hosts more than 17,000 public datasets across core scientific domains , including genomics, protein design, chemistry, weather and climate, Earth observation, and astronomy. That figure approaches 29,000 when medicine and mathematics are included, alongside a comparable number of scientific models.

The pace of sharing is also accelerating. Researchers shared more than three times as many new science datasets on Hugging Face in the first nine months of 2026 as in the same period of 2025 , with growth remaining substantial even after excluding the largest individual uploader.

Figure 1. New public science datasets on Hugging Face per quarter, by domain (Q1 2023–Q3 2026). Counts datasets still public, by creation date. Source: Hugging Face Hub data, October 2026. Explore the data .

When organizations share research in reusable formats, the scientific community can build on it at scale. The 18 public repositories maintained by NIH's National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) on Hugging Face have collectively received more than 11 million downloads, while NASA IMPACT's 27 repositories have received approximately 770,000 downloads, as of October 26, 2026. Documentation is also an important part of making these resources useful: 90% of dataset downloads on Hugging Face are from fully documented datasets .

Publicly available genomic data has proved important in contributing to research that further advances fields such as biological research; researchers at Hugging Face have been building on openly available scientific resources, including recent releases from HuggingFaceBio such as Carbon-A and Carbon-X . By releasing the resulting models, datasets, and tools openly, these efforts demonstrate how existing scientific resources can support new research that others can build upon.

This is the kind of activity that we are further catalyzing via Project ProtoStar through institutional policies adopted by participating orgs. As an early example of institutional commitment, CMU's Open Source Programs Office is encouraging its researchers to share suitable datasets, AI models, and other research outputs on Hugging Face, while recognizing the continued importance of domain-specific repositories.

Making scientific artifacts AI-ready is an important first step. We also want to demonstrate what researchers, developers, and the broader scientific community can accomplish when those resources are made available for reuse.

A central question for ProtoStar is: Can publicly funded scientific datasets, models, and code, released in AI-ready formats, be readily discovered, reused, combined, and extended to accelerate scientific discovery and public benefit?

To explore this, ProtoStar will organize a series of open challenges, each hosted by a participating research institution and built around scientific resources that the institution has released openly. The challenges have two complementary goals:

The resulting projects and lessons learned will help build a practical evidence base for making publicly funded science more accessible and useful.

Hosted by Carnegie Mellon University | November 2–13, 2026

The inaugural ProtoStar challenge invites participants to test whether AI can improve predictions of urban climate conditions using historical weather data from 210 U.S. cities. Building on research by Carnegie Mellon University , teams will use climate records through 2018 to predict actual conditions from 2019 to 2026, allowing their models to be evaluated against observed weather rather than hypothetical future scenarios.

Participants will forecast four indicators relevant to urban planning: average annual temperature, total annual precipitation, the hottest day of the year, and cooling degree days, a measure of demand for air conditioning. Their predictions will be compared against simple statistical baselines, including historical averages and linear trends, to assess whether AI approaches offer meaningful improvements in accuracy.

Beyond forecasting, participants will also propose a short climate adaptation policy idea informed by what they learned from the data. This component encourages teams to connect scientific analysis with practical public benefits, such as preparing cities for extreme heat, improving energy efficiency, or managing changing precipitation patterns.

Teams will submit a Hugging Face dataset with these outputs. Forecasting performance will be assessed through a public leaderboard measuring prediction errors against established baselines, while policy ideas will receive separate consideration. Final forecasting results will be published in early 2027, once the complete 2026 weather records are available.

Explore the CMU Climate Risk Intelligence Challenge

The CMU challenge is the first in this series. Other participating institutions will host their own challenges sequentially, each highlighting different publicly funded scientific resources and opportunities for reuse. Future challenges will be announced through the Project ProtoStar page on Hugging Face .

Whether you're an academic researcher, student, independent developer, or company building on open scientific infrastructure, ProtoStar offers opportunities to put publicly funded research to work and help us learn what is needed to make AI-ready open science more widely useful.

We also welcome universities, federal research agencies, national laboratories, nonprofits, and other research organizations interested in making their scientific resources more accessible and reusable. To explore participation or collaboration, reach out to protostar@orcaopen.org .

Our hope is that ProtoStar will make it easier for publicly funded scientific work to reach the people and tools that can build on it, while generating practical evidence about the infrastructure and practices needed to support open science at scale.

Mistral Large 4 (aka Le Chonk) is a multimodal, multilingual, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model from Mistral. It takes text and images as input and generates text. It has about 1T total, 49B active parameter , and a context window of 1M tokens .

The model is released in two official variants:

There are also GGUFs created by Unsloth and the llama.cpp team. It’s distributed under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (an MIT derivative that establishes limitations for model-as-a-service offerings).

Mistral Large 4 is particularly strong for cybersecurity, coding agents, and multimodality. In this post, we look at how the model works, its capabilities, architecture and more!

Mistral Large 4 combines a large pool of experts with sparse attention and a Pixtral vision encoder. The language model selects a small group of experts for each token, while its attention indexer selects which earlier token positions to attend to. These are two different forms of sparsity, where one selects feed-forward networks, the other selects context positions.

You can find all the checkpoints in the Mistral Large 4 collection .

Mistral Large 4 scores 82% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index test that asks a model to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch the software. Mistral reports that several closed frontier models score near zero on the same test because they refuse to attempt the work. This is super important for defenders, because fixing a vulnerability usually requires reproducing the vulnerability. In Mistral’s internal testing, Mistral Large 4 was also useful for malware analysis, vulnerability prioritisation and writing detection rules, which the model was not explicitly trained for.

Mistral mainly positions the model for defensive security work. Vulnerability research and incident response often appear like attacks in model input, so closed source filters can block them. A team that depends on an API can also lose access in the middle of an incident. Crucially, open weight models put both the usage policy and the deployment under the user’s control. That said, the model still declines harmful requests: on cyber prompts from JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT and AgentHarm, its average refusal rate is higher than any other open weight model.

For community builders, an open weight model like Mistral Large 4 unlocks a load of downstream use cases. You could build your own cyber system around your code base, crash logs, and malware samples. For example, with TRL you could fine-tune smaller models from Mistral Large 4 traces patching your code base. In fact, reproduce-then-patch tasks use a verifiable reward, so it fits with RL environments that could be used to further RL smaller security models. Open weights also let researchers measure the model’s refusal behaviour directly instead of relying on the provider’s description.

In short, cyber capabilities like ML4’s in the open are a huge boost for the community.

We have interviewed Pierre Stock about the cyber capabilities of the model, you can watch it here .

Mistral Large 4’s text decoder has 72 layers, a hidden dimension of 6,144, and 64 attention heads. Its attention blocks combine Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) with a DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) indexer (a direction in other models such as GLM 5.3). MLA keeps a compressed KV representation, and DSA selects up to 2,048 key positions for each query.

For each decoder block, there’s a 3:1 RoPE to NoPE pattern, i.e. 3 decoder layers employ RoPE and every fourth layer uses NoPE. The model also shares KV state across layers. The first decoder layer uses a dense feed-forward network. The other 71 layers use MoE blocks, in which a softmax router selects four of the 128 experts for each token. One shared expert always runs alongside the selected experts, for a total of 5 active experts per token.

Regarding RoPE, Mistral uses LeRope , a YaRN-scaled RoPE with one learned multiplier per frequency.

Mistral Large 4 employs a 1.6B Pixtral encoder. Pixtral has 30 layers, a hidden dimension of 2,048, and 16 attention heads. It uses 14 × 14 patches and a patch-merge projector with spatial merge size 2. You can see the encoder pipeline below.

Mistral Large 4 delivers strong benchmark performance across coding, cybersecurity, multimodal understanding, and agentic workflows, positioning it as a competitive addition to the open-weight ecosystem. As of October 29, 2026, the model is the fifth best open weights model on Artificial Analysis Intelligence index.

On coding, ML4 achieves 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1 , 59.4% on SWE-Atlas-QnA , and 28.3% on Terminal-Bench 4 . Its combined Coding Agent Index score of 49.8% places it ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 and Qwen3.8 Max.

Coding capabilities of ML4 extend to knowledge work, with 59.9% on AutomationBench and 1,393 Elo on AA-Briefcase , which evaluate business workflows and long-horizon professional tasks.

Cybersecurity is one of Mistral Large 4’s standout capabilities, with strong results across real-world vulnerability assessment and security competition tasks. Three benchmarks highlight the model’s cyber performance:

Mistral Large 4 also demonstrates 93.3% attack resistance on Lakera’s B3 benchmark , adding evidence of robustness against prompt-injection attacks. Beyond benchmarks, internal testing showed promising results in malware analysis, vulnerability prioritization, and detection-rule generation.

The default is high , and note that reasoning cannot be disabled, so using reasoning_effort : none would still use high .

Language models can do a lot. They write, summarize, translate, and call tools. But they're only a small part of what machine learning can do.

Say a customer calls your support line. First, you want to know what they said (speech recognition). Then, you want to decide where to send them (decision). You could hand both to a language model, but there are models built for each that are better, faster, and less expensive.

In our AnyLanguageModel 1.0 recap , we looked at a year of local and hosted models in Swift. With AnyLanguageModel and swift-huggingface now on their 1.x releases, we're extending the same approach to speech and decisions: familiar Swift APIs with a choice of model.

Both packages can download open models from the Hugging Face Hub and run them on device.

Computers have been transcribing speech for decades, and in the past few years, they've gotten very good at it. Apple platforms already have an API for it. macOS 26 and iOS 26 introduced SpeechAnalyzer , Apple's new speech-to-text API. You add modules such as SpeechTranscriber and SpeechDetector to an analyzer, give it a file or a stream of audio buffers, and read results from async sequences as they arrive. AssetInventory installs the models, so your app decides when downloads happen.

It's a well-designed API, but the only engine behind it is Apple's. AnySpeechRecognizer keeps the API and lets you choose the engine:

The package mirrors SpeechAnalyzer , SpeechTranscriber , DictationTranscriber , SpeechDetector , and AssetInventory , with Apple's Speech framework as the default engine. If your code uses that shared API, changing the import is enough. To use Parakeet instead, change only how you create the transcriber:

The steps for installing assets, running the analyzer, and reading results stay the same. The README has a complete example and lists the differences from Apple's framework.

Parakeet v3 is NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 . It's a polyglot: it recognizes 25 European languages and works out which one it's hearing, so you don't pass a locale.

Parakeet Ultra is Moondream's post-trained take on v3 . It was more accurate in most of our measurements.

Parakeet Unified is NVIDIA's English-only Parakeet .

All three Parakeets run on the package's own Core ML runtime, which supports file and live input, volatile results, word timing, and word confidence.

Qwen3-ASR is Alibaba's speech model, in 0.6B and 1.7B sizes. It recognizes 30 languages and 22 Chinese dialects, including Mandarin, Cantonese, Japanese, and Korean, which Parakeet doesn't cover. It detects the language automatically, or you can set one:

Qwen3-ASR gives one final result for each segment of up to 40 seconds, without volatile results, word timing, or confidence. It runs on the GPU and is slower than Parakeet, so it's better suited to transcribing files than live input.

To add another engine, implement SpeechRecognitionModel for its configuration and SpeechRecognitionExecutor for one module's session. The README includes a small provider that reports placeholder text to help you get started.

To run these models in apps, we converted them to Core ML and published them on the Hub:

Each repository records its source checkpoint and a checksum for every file, and the package pins it to a fixed revision. The Parakeet repositories add an 8-second encoder for live input, which cuts live analysis time by about a third at the cost of a somewhat higher word error rate. The repository also has the conversion workflows, most of which follow FluidInference's mobius scripts, and checks each conversion against the original model.

Downloads happen only when your app asks for them: about 600 MB for each Parakeet, plus about 590 MB for the live encoder, 0.9 to 2.4 GB for Qwen3-ASR, and about 250 MB for Sortformer. Files go in the standard Hugging Face cache, so a Mac app outside the sandbox shares them with Python and other Hugging Face tools.

When you transcribe a conversation, you often want to know who said what. That's speaker diarization, and Apple's Speech framework doesn't have a module for it, so AnySpeechRecognizer adds one. SpeakerDiarizer runs NVIDIA's Streaming Sortformer on Core ML alongside an Apple or Parakeet transcriber, on the same timeline:

The diarizer tracks up to four speakers, even when they talk over each other. A SpeakerTimeline collects its results and attributes each timed word to a speaker, so you can print a transcript by speaker turn. Like image support in AnyLanguageModel, this goes beyond what Apple's API offers today.

The diarizer uses Sortformer v2 by default. You can also choose v2.1 , which NVIDIA trained with more meeting data and which was more accurate on meetings in our measurements, too.

We measured the package with its hear command-line tool on an M4 Max Mac Studio with macOS 27.0.1. Here are the word error rates on LibriSpeech files of 3 to 8 minutes:

Parakeet transcribes an hour of audio in about 20 to 40 seconds from a file, or about 1.5 to 2.5 minutes live, with about 100 MB of memory once Core ML has compiled the model. Qwen3-ASR is much slower and needs a few gigabytes of memory. Meetings are hard for everyone: on AMI recordings, where people talk over each other, every engine we tested had a word error rate above 23%.

These numbers come from one machine and a few datasets, so measure with your own hardware and audio. hear evaluate works on your own files, and the repository's natural-speech-eval.py tool reproduces these measurements . So far, we've tested only on macOS 27, not on an iPhone.

Next, we'd like to add more engines, including Core AI on macOS 27 and iOS 27.

AnyDecisionModel is a different story. There's no Apple framework to map onto, and decision models aren't new, exactly.

It's only a decision model if it comes from the Décision region of France; otherwise, it's sparkling zero-shot classification.

What's new is the name, a lot of hype, and a crop of models trained to make decisions. We think that's where things are going, so we wanted a Swift API that's ready for them.

Apps often ask language models to make decisions. Is this message urgent? Which team should handle this ticket? How frustrated is this customer? The usual approach is to prompt a language model and parse the text that it generates. That gives you one answer, but doesn't show the probabilities it assigned to the alternatives.

Here's what a decision looks like in Swift:

urgent is a Double . team is a Choice containing the selected case, a probability for each option, and a confidence value. anger is a Score containing the expected level, a probability for each level, and a confidence value. Because Department conforms to Choosable , team.value is a Department that you can use in an exhaustive switch .

If you've used Foundation Models or AnyLanguageModel, the model-and-session pattern will look familiar. A DecisionSession holds a single state, which can be text or JSON, and every question is about that state. Questions are independent: an answer never becomes input to a later question. To ask several questions at once, pass them to decide(_:) as a batch.

For each question, the MLX backend builds a prompt with a one-token label for each allowed answer, then reads the probability of each label from one forward pass.

Emoji Magnet is a macOS app with a text field above a pile of 343 emoji. Type a phrase, such as "things you wear", and the emoji that match rise out of the pile. Refine it to "things you wear in winter", and the emoji that no longer match fall back.

The app has no built-in keyword rules; the model decides everything at inference time. When you pause typing, it asks the model one yes-or-no question for each emoji, for example:

The session's state holds the phrase. The demo above uses the hosted Jev backend, which answers all 343 questions in one request, so the emoji settle in about half a second for each phrase. Without a TYPESAFE_AI_API_KEY , the app runs Qwen3 4B on your Mac with the MLX backend. That backend uses prefix caching to evaluate the state once, then answers 16 questions per forward pass. On an M4 Max, a group of 16 takes about 0.45 seconds after the model loads. A full pass over all 343 emoji takes about 10 seconds, and each group's results appear as soon as they arrive.

Emoji Magnet is in the AnyDecisionModel-Examples repository.

Reading next-token probabilities works with general-purpose language models, but those models weren't trained to make decisions. Cloudflare's Clef models are an example of a newer approach: a model with a trained decision head that turns a state and a schema of typed questions into decisions, returning probabilities for all allowed options across the questions in one forward pass. Clef-Flash is the 9B variant.

AnyDecisionModel runs Clef-Flash on a Mac with MLX:

You use the same sessions and questions, but MLXHeadDecisionModel reads each decision from Clef's trained decision head instead of from next-token probabilities. The 4-bit model is a 6.2 GB download, and its model card recommends a Mac with at least 16 GB of memory. Clef can read images and video, but this backend accepts only text and JSON states.

Raw probabilities from language models are often overconfident. The local backends accept a Calibration , which applies a temperature to every answer and a bias to yes-or-no answers. Use separate datasets to fit the calibration and evaluate the results.

Language models can also favor an option because of its position in a list. On the MLX, Core AI, and llama.cpp next-token backends, turn on rotationDebiasing to ask a choice question once for each rotation of the options and average the probabilities. That costs one prompt evaluation per rotation.

Each local choice and score also includes a confidence value based on the entropy of its probabilities. It measures how concentrated the probabilities are, not whether the answer is right, so check the error rate on your own data before you pick a threshold. The next-token backends' diagnostics report how much probability the model assigned to the allowed answers. A low value means it assigned most of the probability elsewhere.

The next-token backends label answers "yes" and "no", A to Z, or 0 to 9, so a choice can have at most 26 options, and a score at most 10 levels. Decision heads have no such limit.

Like AnyLanguageModel, the package uses Swift package traits. Without traits, it has no third-party dependencies. You get the core types and the Jev and Ollama backends, which also build on Linux. Enable the MLX , CoreAI , or Llama trait for the local backends.

Both packages require Swift 6.2 or later and macOS 26 or iOS 26 or later. The Parakeet and Sortformer runtimes and the MLX backend require Apple silicon. AnyDecisionModel's MLX build tasks use Xcode's Swift 6.4 or later and the Metal toolchain; Core AI requires Xcode 27 and an OS 27 runtime.

Add the packages to your Package.swift :

For now, AnyDecisionModel's CoreAI trait can't be combined with AnySpeechRecognizer, because coreai-kit 0.7.3 requires swift-huggingface below 1.0 and AnySpeechRecognizer requires 1.x.

Each README has more examples and details about requirements and backends. AnySpeechRecognizer also includes a command-line tool, hear , that transcribes local files, labels their speakers, and evaluates the results. Every hear command requires --backend apple , --backend parakeet , or --backend qwen ; run hear prepare with the same backend and model options before analysis to install the needed assets.

Try them in your apps and tell us what works and what doesn't. Issues and pull requests are welcome on both repositories.

Thanks to NVIDIA for Parakeet, Sortformer, and NeMo, to Moondream for Parakeet Ultra, to FluidInference, whose FluidAudio and mobius projects documented the conventions that the Parakeet runtime and the Core ML conversions follow, to Cloudflare for Clef, and to everyone who contributed to AnyLanguageModel, whose patterns both packages borrow.

MN202610_nqx14dpxl7.t:
Amerika yafatiye ibihano minisiteri y'ingabo z'u Rwanda na banki ya Zigama CSS igenewe abasirikare n'abandi bakora mu nzego z'umutekano n'ubutasi, kubera uruhare bashinjwa rwo gufasha umutwe w'inyeshyamba wa M23 mu burasirazuba bwa Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (DRC).

Ibi byongereye igitutu ku butegetsi bw'u Rwanda cyo gucyura ingabo rushinjwa kohereza ku butaka bwa DRC no guhagarika ubufasha rushinjwa guha izo nyeshyamba, ubu ziri mu mutwe mushya wa FRN watangajwe muri uku kwezi. FRN iyobowe n'uwahoze ari Perezida wa DRC Joseph Kabila, ikaba ishaka gukuraho ubutegetsi bwa DRC.

U Rwanda ruhakana gufasha izo nyeshyamba no kohereza ingabo ku butaka bwa DRC, rukavuga ko rwashyizeho "ingamba z'ubwirinzi".

Minisitiri w'imari w'Amerika Scott Bessent yagize ati: "U Rwanda rugomba guhagarika ubufasha bwarwo kuri M23 no gukura ingabo zarwo mu burasirazuba bwa DRC."

Amerika ifashe ibi bihano nyuma y'igihe kigera hafi ku mwaka u Rwanda na DRC bisinye amasezerano y'amahoro yahagarikiwe n'Amerika agamije kurangiza iyo ntambara.

Bikurikiye kandi ibihano Amerika yafatiye ingabo z'u Rwanda (RDF) hamwe n'abajenerali bane barimo n'umugaba mukuru w'ingabo, muri Werurwe (3) uyu mwaka.

Imirwano yarakomeje mu burasirazuba bwa DRC kuva muri Mutarama (1) mu 2025, ubwo M23 yafataga umujyi wa Goma, ikanafata umujyi wa Bukavu muri Gashyantare (2) uwo mwaka.

Minisiteri y'imari y'Amerika ivuga ko minisiteri y'ingabo z'u Rwanda yategetse abasirikare babarirwa mu bihumbi kurwana ku ruhande rwa M23 mu burasirazuba bwa DRC, igatanga intwaro, ibikoresho n'imyitozo.

M23 yafashe uturere dukungahaye ku mabuye y'agaciro mu ntara ya Kivu ya Ruguru na Kivu y'Epfo, turimo n'ibirombe by'amabuye y'agaciro muri Kivu y'Epfo n'ibirombe bya Rubaya bicukurwamo coltan nyinshi muri Kivu ya Ruguru.

Washington ivuga ko amabuye y'agaciro acukurwa ahagenzurwa n'izo nyeshyamba avangwa n'andi mabuye y'u Rwanda, ikavuga ko u Rwanda rwohereza mu mahanga amabuye menshi cyane kurusha ayo rucukura mu butaka bwarwo.

Mu gihe cyashize, u Rwanda rwahakanye gusahura umutungo kamere wa DRC urimo n'amabuye y'agaciro, rushimangira ko rufite amabuye y'agaciro menshi.

Amerika ivuga ko ibi bihano bigamije gushimangira amasezerano ya Washington Perezida w'u Rwanda Paul Kagame na Perezida wa DRC Félix Tshisekedi basinye mu Kuboza (12) mu 2025, ku buhuza bw'Amerika. Ayo masezerano agamije kurangiza iyo ntambara no kwagura ubucuruzi n'ishoramari mu karere, ariko imirwano yarakomeje.

Ku itariki ya 24 y'uku kwezi kw'Ukwakira (10), mbere yuko ibyo bihano bitangazwa, Perezida Tshisekedi yashishikarije amahanga kongera igitutu ku Rwanda.

Yagize ati: "Tugomba gusaba dushimitse ko amahanga afatira ibihano bifatika u Rwanda no kurwotsa igitutu kurushaho, kugira ngo amaherezo dushobore kubona amahoro arambye mu gihugu cyacu."

Mu itangazo yahaye ibiro ntaramakuru Reuters, minisiteri y'ububanyi n'amahanga ya DRC yishimiye ibyo bihano ndetse ishishikariza u Rwanda kubahiriza ibyo rwiyemeje mu masezerano ya Washington, kubahiriza ibikubiye mu mahame-remezo y'Umuryango w'Abibumbye no gukura ingabo zarwo ku butaka bwa DRC.

Umuvugizi wa leta y'u Rwanda Yolande Makolo yabwiye BBC ati: "Amasezerano ya Washington arimo ibyiyemejwe byumvikana bijyanye n'umutekano w'u Rwanda, by'umwihariko irandurwa ry'umutwe wa jenoside wa FDLR ufashwa na DR Congo, bitarashyirwa mu bikorwa na gato, kandi bitaryozwa [DR Congo]."

FDLR ni umutwe ufitanye isano n'abashinjwa kuba barakoze jenoside yabaye mu Rwanda mu mwaka wa 1994. U Rwanda ruvuga ko uwo mutwe uteje inkeke ku mutekano warwo ndetse ruvuga ko kuba uwo mutwe uba mu burasirazuba bwa DRC ari yo mpamvu rufata "ingamba z'ubwirinzi".

Makolo yagize ati: "U Rwanda rukomeje kuba rwiteguye gushyira mu bikorwa mu buryo bwuzuye Amasezerano ya Washington, bikabera icyarimwe n'uko DRC ishyira mu bikorwa mu buryo bwuzuye ibyo yiyemeje, ndetse umuhuza akabaza inshingano impande zose."

Amerika yanafatiye ibihano banki ya Zigama CSS.

Amerika ivuga ko iyo banki yatumye habaho ihererekanywa rya miliyoni zibarirwa muri za mirongo z'amadolari y'Amerika zijya muri M23 no mu ishami ryayo rya politike (AFC), ifasha mu kugurira RDF ibikoresho bya gisirikare mu Bushinwa ndetse ko yatumye zahabu ivanwa mu turere tugenzurwa n'izo nyeshyamba ikajyanwa i Kigali.

Ibyo bihano bifatira imitungo y'abarebwa na byo hashingiwe ku mategeko y'Amerika ndetse muri rusange bibuza Abanyamerika n'abo muri Amerika n'ibikorwa by'ubucuruzi byaho cyangwa byabo gukorana n'abafatiwe ibihano, keretse igihe byaba bibanje gutangirwa uruhushya n'Amerika cyangwa hakabaho gusonerwa. Kurenga kuri ibyo bihano bishobora gutuma habaho gufatirwa ibihano ku bo muri Amerika no ku banyamahanga.

Izo ngamba zikurikiye ibindi bihano Amerika yafatiye RDF n'abajenerali bane muri Werurwe (3) mu 2026. Muri Kamena (6) mu 2026, Amerika yanafatiye ibihano kompanyi enye zicukura amabuye y'agaciro zo mu Rwanda, zirimo kompanyi imwe yitwa Gasabo Gold Refinery LTD (inazwi nka Gasabo Gold) itunganya zahabu, zishinjwa gukora ubucuruzi bwa magendu bw'amabuye y'agaciro ava mu ntambara.

Igitutu kirimo no kwiyongera mu masezerano mu by'imikino u Rwanda rwagiranye n'amakipe yo mu mahanga. Abasenateri babiri bo muri Amerika bashishikarije shampiyona y'Amerika ya Basketball (NBA) kongera gutekereza ku mubano wayo w'ubucuruzi ifitanye n'u Rwanda, bibaza niba uhuje n'ibyo NBA itangaza ko yiyemeje byo kurengera uburenganzira bwa muntu.

Mu ibaruwa bandikiye umukuru wa NBA Adam Silver ku itariki ya 23 Ukwakira (10) uyu mwaka, senateri Jeff Merkley na senateri Marsha Blackburn bibajije ku bufatanye NBA ikomeje kugirana n'u Rwanda mu gihe rushinjwa guhonyora uburenganzira bwa muntu.

Nta gisubizo gifatika NBA iratanga kuri iyo baruwa.

U Rwanda rumaze igihe rukoresha amasezerano yo mu mikino rugirana n'amakipe akomeye, mu rwego rwo kuzamura igihagararo cyarwo mu mahanga. Muri uku kwezi, u Rwanda rwageze ku masezerano y'imyaka 10 yo kwakira amarushanwa mpuzamahanga yo gusiganwa mu modoka zizwi nka Formula 1, guhera "mu ntangiriro ya za 2030", azitwa African Grand Prix.

Amasezerano u Rwanda rwari rufitanye n'ikipe ya Arsenal yarangiye mu 2026, mu gihe ikipe ya Bayern Munich na yo mu 2025 yarangije amasezerano y'ubucuruzi yari ifitanye n'u Rwanda muri gahunda yo kurwamamaza ya 'Visit Rwanda', ivuga ko amasezerano izakomezanya na rwo azibanda ku guteza imbere abafite impano.

MN202610_zzpuzgirga.t:
Umunyarwanda yakatiwe muri Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika, nyuma yo guhamwa n'icyaha cyo kubeshya ubutabera ku ruhare rwe muri jenoside yabaye mu Rwanda mu 1994, mu rubanza rw'uwahoze ari mugenzi we biganaga muri kaminuza.

Inteko y'abacamanza bo mu rukiko rwa leta i Boston yahamije Eric Nshimiye, ufite imyaka 54, ibyaha byo kubeshya ubutabera no kubangamira imikorere y'ubutabera. Ibyo byaturutse ku buhamya yatanze mu rubanza rwo mu 2019 ruregwamo uburiganya mu by'abinjira n'abasohoka bwari bwaregwagamo Jean Leonard Teganya, na we washinjwaga kugira uruhare muri genocide.

Nshimiye yahunze u Rwanda ajya muri Kenya mu 1994, nyuma aza kwemererwa kwinjira muri Amerika nk'impunzi mu mwaka wakurikiyeho wa 1995.

Abantu bagera ku 800.000 bahitanywe na genocide, kandi abenshi muri bo bakaba bari Abatutsi. Abo bose bishwe n'abahezanguni b'Abahutu mu gihe cya jenoside yamaze iminsi 100 mu Rwanda mu 1994.

Ubushinjacyaha bwavuze ko Eric Nshimiye yahishe amakuru ajyanye n'uruhare rwe muri jenoside kugira ngo abashe kwemererwa kwinjira muri Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika.

Ibimenyetso byatanzwe mu rubanza rwe byagaragaje ko, ubwo yari umunyeshuri muri Kaminuza y'u Rwanda i Butare, yagize uruhare mu bitero byagabwaga ku Batutsi, harimo no kubakubita ubuhiri mu mutwe.

Nshimiye ashobora gukatirwa kugeza ku myaka itanu y'igifungo kuri buri kimwe mu byaha bine byo kubeshya ubutabera, ndetse akazahanishwa igifungo gishobora kugera ku myaka 10 ku cyaha cyo kubangamira ubutabera.

Ateganyijwe gukatirwa ku wa 26 Mutarama (1) 2027.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Umushinjacyaha wo muri Minisiteri y'Ubutabera ya Amerika, Tysen Duva, yagize ati: "Mu gihe cyegereye imyaka 30, uyu mugabo yahishe uruhare rwe muri genoside yabaye mu Rwanda mu 1994 n'ibikorwa by'urugomo ndengakamere yakoze, harimo no gukubita abantu kugeza bapfuye akoresheje ubuhiri."

Yakomeje agira ati: "Nyuma yabeshye abashinzwe abinjira n'abasohoka kugira ngo ahabwe ubwenegihugu bwa Amerika, kandi anabeshya inteko y'abacamanza b'urukiko rwa leta mu rwego rwo kwirwanaho no kurengera undi muntu ukekwaho kuba yaragize uruhare muri genoside yo mu Rwanda."

Umunyamategeko wa Nshimiye, Kurt Kerns, yatangaje ko ababajwe n'umwanzuro w'urukiko kandi ko bazakoresha inzira zose zemewe n'amategeko kugira ngo bawujuririre.

Mu ijambo rye ribanza mu rubanza rwabaye mu kwezi k'Ukwakira (10), Kerns yavuze ko ibyo birego bishingiye ku "byaha byahimbwe", ashimangira ko Nshimiye atari i Butare igihe ibikorwa by'ubwicanyi byatangiraga.

Yanavuze ko Nshimiye yashinjwe nyuma yo gutanga ubuhamya bushimangira imyitwarire myiza ya Jean Leonard Teganya, wahoze ari mugenzi we muri kaminuza.

Teganya yakatiwe imyaka umunani y'igifungo mu mwaka wa 2019 nyuma yo guhamwa n'icyaha cy'uburiganya bukomeye mu bijyanye n'abinjira n'abasohoka, aho ubushinjacyaha bwavuze ko yabeshye ku ruhare rwe muri jenoside.

Yashinjwaga kandi kugira uruhare nibura mu bwicanyi burindwi no gufata abagore ku ngufu inshuro eshanu, ariko we yakomeje guhakana ko yagize uruhare muri jenoside.

MN202610_1xz1kxluhef.t:
Neema Munuo, whose 18-year-old daughter Maria Chami was shot dead on the day of the election, wants the government to acknowledge her suffering

Families affected by election-related violence in Tanzania that led to the deaths of at least 500 people a year ago have told the BBC they want justice for those killed in the protests and help with medical expenses for those injured.

"We can no longer afford to pay hospital bills," Meshack Sane, who was shot in the leg, told the BBC.

On the eve of the anniversary of the poll that saw President Samia Suluhu Hassan elected with 98% of the vote, rights group Amnesty International also accused her government of "weaponising counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear".

The opposition dismissed the result as a "mockery" of democracy as Samia's two main challengers were excluded.

Tundu Lissu, the 58-year-old leader of the main opposition Chadema party, had been put on trial for treason ahead of the poll - preventing him from standing.

He had been demanding electoral reforms and a verdict in his case is due next week.

Earlier this week, Lissu went on a hunger strike as he was not being allowed access to his lawyers - an allegation the prison authorities denied.

His lawyer Dickson Matata told the BBC on Wednesday he had now been granted a meeting and would be eating again.

A government-appointed commission of inquiry said 518 people had died from "unnatural causes" during the unrest, including 197 who were shot dead

In its statement, Amnesty said it had documented how over the past year security agencies had committed human rights violations with impunity against government critics, opposition supporters, media organisations and dissenting members of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party.

"Not a single official has been criminally investigated, let alone prosecuted and punished for the excessive force that Tanzanian security forces used against protesters," said Tigere Chagutah, the group's regional director for East and southern Africa

"In fact, the situation has only deteriorated since the crackdown began. In a classic tactic pulled out of the authoritarian playbook, the authorities are increasingly weaponising counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear."

The authorities in the East African nation have repeatedly denied accusations of widespread abuses and say the government is committed to respecting human rights.

Samia, 66, has insisted the election was fair and transparent and blamed foreigners for the unrest, saying it was part of a plot to overthrow her.

Last year, the BBC verified multiple videos of police shooting towards protesters. Footage posted online showed demonstrators being confronted by heavily armed units blocking their progress and firing tear gas to disperse crowds.

Meshack Sane says he has already had five operations on his injured leg - but cannot afford further treatment

The BBC has since spoken to families of some of the victims of the electoral violence, who are still seeking answers.

Many, like Mwajuma Hamisi, have been left destitute. Her husband George Kisivani was shot in the northern city of Arusha on 29 October 2025, the day of the vote, and died two days later.

"I lost my husband, upon whom we, a family with five children, depended. We now have no other source of support. I am left to fight for the family on my own. We have no other assistance," the 32-year-old told the BBC.

She now sells vegetables at a nearby market to support the family - and would like help from the government.

Sane, who shot in the leg in Arusha, has been suffering physically and financially.

The father of three says he has undergone more than five major operations to deal with the gunshot wound. He still needs further surgery but says he can no longer afford treatment.

"We have done everything within our means, but we have reached our limit," the 33-year-old told the BBC.

"The government should look into the situation of those of us who have suffered these tragedies, so that we can receive medical treatment, as some of us are still very sick."

He explained how in the wake of the violence hospitals initially refused to treat injured people.

In the intervening months, his relatives have sought help from local officials and the district commissioner, but he says they were told the government had not allocated a budget for victims of the violence.

The BBC has not independently verified his account of those conversations.

A commission of inquiry's report into the violence was handed to President Samia in April, officially recording 518 deaths.

But Amnesty has criticised the fact that the full report has not yet been made public, saying it "entrenches a culture of secrecy".

The president has since set up another commission to inquiry to identify those behind the violence.

"It is imperative that this new commission comprehensively address the role of security forces in the election-related crackdown," Chagutah said.

President Samia Suluhu Hassan was declared the winner of the 29 October poll with 98% of the vote

The rights group says that between 3 and 17 September 2026, it interviewed 17 people who gave details of a continuing crackdown by the authorities.

Some of them were targeted after demonstrations were called for 7 July to demand democratic reforms and justice for those killed last year.

These marches were banned by the authorities. A 26-year-old man who had expressed support told Amnesty how he was arrested on 24 July in Dar es Salaam and held without charge for 47 days.

He said he was blindfolded by his interrogators who wanted to know who was funding the protests and threatened to kill him.

"On the first day, they didn't give me food. When I asked for water, they urinated on my blindfolded face and said, 'That is the price for those of you opening your mouths to make noise'," he said.

"On the second day, I was taken to Gogoni police station where they beat your legs until they get numb but then insist that you must stand."

The right groups also cites other "acts that may amount to torture... arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances and abductions".

The authorities did not respond to the BBC's or Amnesty's request for comment.

Many of those who lost relatives a year ago want the government to acknowledge their suffering and address their questions about justice, like 40-year-old Neema Munuo.

She says her grief over the death of her 18-year-old daughter Maria Chami, who had gone out to buy phone credit in Arusha when she was shot, has often left her too distraught to leave the house.

"It is a date I will never forget for the rest of my life, because whenever I recall it, I feel as though I am burning inside," Munuo told the BBC.

This feeling resonates with farmer Juma Nasibu, who lives near the city of Mwanza on the shores of Lake Victoria.

He has not seen his 25-year-old nephew Juma Shabani since the unrest.

The young man had been at a cinema hall in the evening when his uncle later heard unconfirmed reports that he was amongst people rounded up and shot. His family have fruitlessly searched for him at hospitals, police stations and prisons.

"To date, what still pains me is that we were never able to recover the body," Nasibu told the BBC.
